cycles.name: Bedrock
focuses: Rebuild the week around what your body can actually recover from — three loaded days, not five.
Groove a trunk-supported hinge so your lower back earns the barbell back next cycle.
Build your first ever cardio base and a daily ten-minute back routine.

paragraphs: You've been training five days a week and going hard, and nothing has moved. That's not because you haven't tried. Your body has been getting a lot of stress and not much room to recover, so it's been holding on instead of changing.

So this month we do something that will feel strange. Three real gym days instead of five, a little lighter than you're used to, and we add walking. This block is about building the floor. We're not chasing the scale yet.

By the end of four weeks I want three things from you: you turned up, your back felt good on every hinge, and your walk got longer each week. Get those and the next block can do the fat loss properly.
outcomes: Every hinge session finished pain free
A real working weight found and logged on every exercise
Four weeks of the daily back routine done

cycles.name: Slow Burn
focuses: Your first real fat-loss phase, on a routine that finally holds.
A fourth day comes back, and the free hinge returns as a skill.

paragraphs: Last month you told me it was too easy, and your logs said the same thing. Almost no soreness, most sessions sitting around a 5 when we were aiming for 7, and you moving your own weights up because the program wasn't doing it fast enough. Your seated leg curl went from 10 to 24. You were right.

So this month gets harder on purpose. A fourth day comes back, your effort target moves from 7 to 8 on most things, and about a dozen movements are brand new. This is also where the fat loss actually starts, so your food gets its first real change and your walking keeps building.
One thing does not get harder, and that's your back work. The deadlift comes in light and stays light, because it's a skill this month, not a lift to push. Everything else you can attack.
outcomes: Every new movement calibrated and logged by week 2
Weight logged in the app at least twice a week
Walks 2 to 3 minutes longer each week
Deadlift finished every session with a flat back

cycles.name: Metabolic Override
focuses: Push the fat loss properly — this is where the mirror starts to change.
First interval work, on a base you spent nine weeks building.

paragraphs: Cycle 3 is where the mirror starts to change. Nine weeks of walking will have built something under you that most people never bother to build, and next month is where we finally get to spend it.
Your cardio stops being one speed. That's all I'll say.
Finish this month properly and the fun one is yours.

cycles.name: Strength Reclaim
focuses: A planned break from the deficit, spent getting genuinely strong.
The barbell hinge comes back, earned by three clean cycles.

cycles.name: Final Cut
focuses: The last push, on the freshest recovery you'll have had all programme.
Then a planned landing, so what you built actually stays.

cards.title: What You Already Did
cards.body:
Before we talk about this month, look at what you just finished. You logged 11 gym sessions when the target was 10 out of 12. You hit it, in a month that took a lot out of you. Most people would have stopped completely.

Your numbers moved everywhere. Seated leg curl 10 to 24. Leg extension 42 to 57. Leg press 70 to 90 for three straight sets. And your walk went from incline 4 to incline 8, when you had never done any cardio in your life. That walk is the biggest thing that changed all month.

One more, and I mean this. In your last session you told me your back was bothering you after the back extension. That was the best thing you did all cycle. With your back history, if you keep quiet and push through, I'm working blind. You told me, so I could fix it. Telling me never costs you your training. It just changes one thing.

cards.title: Why This Month Is Harder
cards.body:
You said the last one was too easy and your log agreed with you. You barely got sore, and most sessions came in around a 5 when we were aiming for 7. That was my call, not your fault. I didn't know yet how much your body could take, so I built month one careful. Now I know.

Three things change. A fourth gym day comes back. Your effort target goes from 7 to 8 on most exercises, so you should be finishing sets with about 2 good reps left instead of 4. And a lot of the exercises are new, so the whole thing should feel different when you open it.

Your walking keeps going the same way it has been. Add 2 to 3 minutes each week and leave the incline where you have it. Don't start running or doing sprints yet. That's next month's job and it only works if you keep building the base now.

cards.title: Week One, And What An 8 Feels Like
cards.body:
There are about a dozen movements in here you've never done. For week 1 only, work all the new ones at RPE 6 and just learn them. Pick a light weight, get the movement right, and don't chase anything. The number on the card opens from week 2.

Everything you already know goes straight to the number on the card from day one. That's your hip thrust, leg press, both leg curls, leg extension and lat pulldown. You have four weeks of logs on those and you've been going too easy, not too hard.

About that 8, because it's new for you. RPE 8 means you finish the set with about 2 good reps left in you. Not 4. If the last rep still flies up, it was a 6 and the weight needs to go up next set. Your own note last month said 80 on the hip thrust was your hard max. That's the kind of weight an 8 lives at.

cards.title: Your Back, And The Plan For It
cards.body:
You told me the back extension bothered you at the end of last month. So here's exactly what happens to it. Weeks 1 and 2 you do it with just your body weight. In week 3 the weight you finished last month on comes back, as long as your back has been quiet. That weight is the ceiling for the whole month, not a target to beat. If it feels easy, good. That's the point.

The deadlift is your new one and it's the same idea. Light, slow, and you stop the movement where your back is still flat. Not where the floor is.

Normal and fine: muscle burn, being tired, stiff either side of your spine the next day. Keep training through that. Beyond that:

  • Mild ache that fades: finish the set and write it in your log.
  • Ache that builds through the set, or changes how you move: stop that exercise, do the rest of the session without it, message me.
  • Sharp, one sided, or anything running down your leg: stop the session. Message me before your next one.

If your back speaks up twice this month, the deadlift comes out and the back extension stays at body weight. And if it's still there when this month ends, I want you to see a physio before we load it any further. That's not a bad sign, it's just where the line is.

cards.title: Start Weighing In
cards.body:
I've added weight tracking to your habit app and it's already switched on, so there's nothing for you to set up. Open Proof and it's the white card on your Today screen under your habits. The Weigh in button logs it. Tap the card itself and it opens your history.

Do it a few mornings a week, same routine each time. Not every day, and don't chase it.

Last month I told you the scale was the last thing I trusted, and that's still true for a single morning. Your weight moves a kilo on water and food alone, and your medication moves it too. This is different because the app doesn't show you one morning. It draws a 7 day average line, so what you see is the direction, not the noise. That's why logging a few is what makes it worth anything.

Nobody sees this but me. It never goes on the leaderboard, never on the wall, never anywhere near the other athletes. And it is yours to take back whenever you want. You can delete one reading from its row, or wipe the whole history in one tap from Settings, and nothing else in your account changes.

It is also the thing that lets me set your food numbers properly, which is the next step.

cards.title: Food, Step Two
cards.body:
Keep doing the swaps from last month, because they're still the whole game. Change the protein for a leaner version of itself instead of adding protein on top of your meals. Chicken thigh becomes breast. Full fat yoghurt becomes Greek. Three whole eggs plus two whites beats five whole eggs.

Now for the numbers I promised you. I need a week of your weigh-ins first. Once I can see where you actually are, I'll send you a daily protein target and we'll set the rest around it. It'll come during your first week.

Until then don't start counting anything. Just keep swapping and keep weighing in.

cards.title: When A Day Feels Too Much
cards.body:
Four gym days is more than last month, and some weeks it won't happen. You don't cancel, you shrink.

  • Rough day: take 1 off every RPE, but never go below 6. Anything already at 6 stays at 6.
  • Really rough day: do the first main lift and the walk, then go home. That still counts as a session.
  • Short on time: first main lift for 2 sets, then the walk.

You can also do the days in any order that fits your week. If you're only going to get three days in, drop Day 2. That's the upper body one and it's the one that costs you least to miss. Your leg days are where the work is.

cards.title: Your Period Week
cards.body:
Same as last month. You don't plan anything, you just use this.

  • Keep all of it: your walks, Day 3, the stretching, the cable hip abduction, the glute bridges in your warm-ups. Light movement usually helps.
  • Cut to 2 sets and work at RPE 6: hip thrust, leg press, the deadlift, the back extension, the split squat. Six is as low as the app goes, so that's your floor. Move the pattern, don't grind it.
  • Skip completely: the pallof press, the suitcase carry, the plank with shoulder taps. Hard bracing through your stomach isn't worth it on those days.

A cut down day still counts as a session. Log it like normal so I can see your week properly. Back to the numbers on your cards once the week's done.

cards.title: Week 5 Is The Easy One
cards.body:
This month runs five weeks and the last one is deliberately lighter. Same exercises, same sets, less weight.

How to do it: take 1 off every RPE, and never go below 6. So your hip thrust, leg press, leg extension, both leg curls, lat pulldown, push up, pec deck and cable abduction all run at 7 that week. Everything else runs at 6. Take real weight off to get there, don't just pretend.

Hold your walks where week 4 left them. Don't drop sets to make it easier, drop weight. The numbers on your cards come back at the start of next month.
